full_judgment: 9. The opposite party No. 1 (first party) entering appearance contested the Rule by filing a counter-affidavit contending that he purchased  0.16 acres of land of RS Dag No. 145 of RS RS Khatian No. 618 having Mutation Khatian No. 689/5, BS Dag No. 430 of Mouza Sikol, Police Station Bandar, District Chittagong, the case land in 1995 and had been possessing therein by erecting boundary wall. As the present petitioner (second party) was trying to dispossess him from the case land there was apprehension of breach of peace, he filed the Miscellaneous Case No. 262 of 1997 under section 145 of the Code on 17-5-1997 in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong who hearing him called for a report from Bandar Police Station, Chittagong. Bandar Police on investigation found this opposite party No. l(first party) in possession of the case land and that the petitioner (second party) was trying to dispossess him from the case land and that also there was actual apprehension of breach of the peace and accordingly submitted the report on 23-5-1997. The Chief Metropolitan Magistrate considering the enquiry report drew proceedings under section 145 of the Code and directed the parties to maintain status quo in respect of possession in the case land and transferred the case record to the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong for trial and disposal by an order dated 28-5-1997. During the continuance of the order of status quo dated 28-5-1997 the petitioner (second party) on 5-6-1997 dispossessed the opposite party No. 1(first party) from the case land. The opposite party No. 1 on 16-6-1997 filed an application under section 145(4) of the Code informing dispossession sought protection of law. It was further contended that on 26-11-1997 Sarbat Banu and 23 others as plaintiffs instituted Other Class Suit No. 230 of 1997 against Haji Faruk Ahmed and 71 others as defendants in the Third Court of Subordinate Judge, Chittagong for partition in respect of 10.49 acres of land. In the said suit the opposite party No. 1 and the petitioner was impleaded as defendant Nos. 34 and 44 respectively but no order of injunction was passed and, as such, possession in the case land was not regulated by the civil Court. That after 1(one) year 5(five) months of drawing proceedings on 28-5-1997 by the learned Magistrate, on the application of a 3rd party an order of status quo was passed in the said suit on 5-10-1998.
